verses.1: Then Solomon will gather together the elders of Israel, all the leaders of the tribes, the chiefs of the fathers among the Israelites, and bring them before King Solomon in Jerusalem. There they will carry the Ark of the Covenant of Jehovah from the city of David, which is Zion.
verses.2: And all the men of Israel gathered together before King Solomon on the day of the festival. It was the seventh day of the new month.
verses.3: And all the elders of Israel came and placed the Ark in its place.
verses.4: And they carried up the Ark of God, along with the altar and all the sacred objects that were in the altar. The priests and Levites carried these things away.
verses.5: And the king Solomon, and all the tribes of Israel who were summoned to him, offered sacrifices of grain and sheep before the altar. These offerings were not recorded in writing, nor were they measured accurately.
verses.6: And the priests brought the Ark of the Covenant of Jehovah to its place: to Dibir, the house of God, to the holy place where the sacred vessels were kept.
verses.7: For the wings of the locusts spread out towards the place where the tree is located. The locusts then settle on the tree and its branches from above.
verses.8: And the tribes grew in number. The leaders of those tribes saw from the sacred place, on the surface of the earth. But they did not see the edges. They remained there until today.
verses.9: There are only two pieces of stone there, which Moses placed there after Jehovah’s death along with the children of Israel when they left Egypt.
verses.10: And when the priests left the Holy Place, the cloud filled the Temple of Jehovah.
verses.11: And the priests were unable to stand and serve before the cloud, for the glory of Jehovah filled the Temple of Jehovah.
verses.12: Then Solomon said, “Yahweh said to Shechem.”
verses.13: I have built a house for you, a place where you can dwell forever.
verses.14: And the king turned his face toward them and blessed all the people of Israel.
verses.15: And the Lord, the God of Israel, said, “May his words be fulfilled by David, my father, and may he have power over all things.”
verses.16: From the day I led my people, Israel, out of Egypt, I did not choose any city among all the cities of Israel to build my house in. Instead, I chose David to be over my people, Israel.
verses.17: And David, my father, built houses for the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.18: And the LORD said to David, my father: “For you were willing to build a house for me in it. It’s good that you did so, since you were willing to do this.”
verses.19: Only you will not build the house. It will be built by someone who comes from your lineage. He will build the house for me.
verses.20: And Jehovah will carry out His words. I will reign under David, my father, and I will sit on the throne of Israel, just as Jehovah has spoken. I will build a house for Jehovah, the God of Israel.
verses.21: And there he made a place for the Ark of God, where the covenant of Jehovah was made with our ancestors when they were brought out of Egypt.
verses.22: And Solomon stood before the Temple of Yahweh, facing all the people of Israel. He spread out his hands towards heaven.
verses.23: And the LORD God of Israel said, “There is no god like me in all the heavens above and on the earth below. I will keep the covenant and the mercy that I have promised to your servants who worship me with all their hearts.”
verses.24: You have obeyed David, my father, in doing what you were commanded to do. You spoke and acted according to what you said, with your mouth and your hands.
verses.25: And now, LORD, God of Israel, protect your servant David, my father. You commanded him not to marry a woman from before you. Only if your sons follow your ways and go before you, just as you did before me, then will he be able to sit on the throne of Israel.
verses.26: And now, O God of Israel, let it be fulfilled your word, as you have spoken to David, my father.
verses.27: For the God of Israel sits on the earth. Now, the heavens and the skies cannot hold you anymore, even though this house I have built is still there.
verses.28: And I will turn my face toward your worship and toward His sanctuary, O LORD God. I will listen to the prayers of your servants who pray before you today.
verses.29: May your eyes be open to this house, night and day, to the place where you said that my name will be there. So that I can hear the prayers of your servant who prays in that place.
verses.30: And you heard the cry of your servant and of Israel’s people, who were coming to this place. And you heard also the cries from your resting place in heaven. So you listened and forgave them.
verses.31: That one who sins against his neighbor, and then brings that sinner before the priest in this house.
verses.32: And you shall hear from heaven, and you shall judge your servants according to their deeds. You shall judge the wicked to bring them to ruin, and the righteous to their just rewards.
verses.33: In the time of your enemies, Israel, before those who have sinned against you and have returned to you. They will praise your name, and they will pray to you in this house.
verses.34: And you will hear from heaven and forgive the sins of your people, Israel, and their descendants. You will restore them to the land that you gave to their ancestors.
verses.35: In the depths of heaven, they will not be able to find any refuge. They will sin against you and fall into this place. But when they pray to your name, they will be forgiven from their sins.
verses.36: And you will hear from heaven and forgive the sins of your servants and your people, Israel. For you have set forth the right path for them to follow. You have given a blessing upon your land, which you have given to your people as an inheritance.
verses.37: Starvation will occur in the land; there will be chaos and destruction. All touch will cause illness and suffering.
verses.38: Every prayer, every offering that is made for all people, for all the people of Israel who know that someone has touched their hearts and opened their mouths to this temple.
verses.39: And you will hear from the heavens that you have been forgiven and pardoned. You have done what was right, and you have given to man all his ways, as you yourself know. You alone know the heart of every human being.
verses.40: So that you may be feared by all those who live on the earth, those whom You have given to our ancestors.
verses.41: And also to the stranger who is not of your people, Israel. He came from a distant land in order to honor your name.
verses.42: For they will hear your great name, your powerful hand, and your sharp spear. Then they will come and pray to this house.
verses.43: You shall hear from heaven that you have done all those things which the foreigner who called you did. So that all the nations of the earth may know your name, and may see you as Israel’s God. And they will know that your name is given to this house which I built.
verses.44: For your people will go into battle against their enemies along the path you have chosen for them. They will pray to Jehovah through the city you have chosen, and through the house I have built for your name.
verses.45: And you heard the prayers of those in heaven, and their pleas. And you made judgments based on those prayers.
verses.46: For they have sinned against you. After all, no one is without sinning. You have abandoned them and handed them over to the enemy. They will return to the land of the enemy, either far away or close by.
verses.47: And they returned to their hearts to the land where they had been banished. They came back and pleaded with You in that land, saying, “We have sinned; we have done wrong.”
verses.48: And they returned to you with all their hearts and souls, in the land of their exile. They came to you through their own land, which You gave to their ancestors. It was the city that You chose for them, and the house that I built for Your name.
verses.49: And you heard the heavens saying, “Your prayers have been accepted, and your offerings have been accepted. You have done what is right.”
verses.50: And you forgave your people who sinned against you, and all their sins they committed against you. You showed mercy before their faces when they repented.
verses.51: For your people and your land are those that you came out of Egypt from within the framework of the Pharaoh’s prison.
verses.52: May your eyes be open to the place where your servants and the people of Israel dwell. May they listen to all your calls.
verses.53: For you have made them your own people, as it is written by Moses, your servant, when he led our ancestors out of Egypt. Adonai Jehovah.
verses.54: And it happened that Solomon stood before the altar of God, and offered all these prayers and sacrifices. He stood there, with his feet placed on the feet of God’s altar, and his hands spread out towards the heavens.
verses.55: And he stood up and blessed all the people of Israel with a great voice, saying:
verses.56: Blessed is Yahweh, who gave peace to the people of Israel. All His words never failed; not one single word of His good things failed. These were the words spoken by Moses, His servant.
verses.57: May the LORD our God be with us, just as He was with our ancestors. Let Him not abandon us or leave us alone.
verses.58: To follow His commands and keep His laws, rules, and judgments, as our ancestors were commanded to do.
verses.59: And these words of mine shall be made true, those things I have prayed before Jehovah. They shall be carried out by our God, Jehovah, day and night, so that He may judge His servants and the people of Israel. These words shall be fulfilled in every day.
verses.60: So that all the nations of the earth may know that Jehovah is the true God.
verses.61: And may it be a peace in your hearts with our God, that you may follow His laws and keep His commandments, just as today.
verses.62: And the king and all of Israel, along with him, offered sacrifices before Jehovah.
verses.63: And Solomon offered the sacrifices that were required for worshiping Jehovah. He offered forty thousand sheep, two hundred thousand goats, and one hundred and twenty thousand lambs. Then he dedicated the Temple of Jehovah, the King, and all the Israelites.
verses.64: On that day, the king sanctified the area in front of the Temple. He performed the offerings and sacrifices there. He also offered the milk from the sacrifices, just as it was done during the worship of the Serpent, which took place in front of Jehovah’s Temple. This area was too small to accommodate all the offerings and sacrifices.
verses.65: And Solomon did what was right at that time. All Israel also joined together with him in celebrating this festival. A large crowd gathered from all over to come to the Valley of the Kings, before our God, Jehovah. It lasted for seven days.
verses.66: On the eighth day, he sent out the people. They blessed the king, and then they went back to their homes, filled with joy and good heart, because of all the good things that Jehovah had done for David, his servant, and for Israel, his people.
